newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid court expands case against ex-bank governor.
newsitem.headline: Madrid court expands case against ex-bank governor.

text.p: A Madrid court said on Wednesday it had expanded fraud charges against former Bank of Spain governor Mariano Rubio, already accused of influence peddling.
Rubio, Spain's central bank governor from 1984 to 1992, now faces charges of bribery, illegal negotiations with civil servants, falsifying documents and crimes against the Treasury.

Rubio was arrested in May 1994 along with Manuel de la Concha, his former broker and an ex-chairman of the Madrid stock exchange, amid investigations into alleged tax evasion and holding a secret account for illicit stock market investments.
He was later released on bail and charged with using contacts to obtain illegal information relating to a loan granted to Ibercorp bank in 1991.
The scandal was one of a series that led to the downfall of the former Socialist government, which lost a general election last March after 13 years of rule.
On Wednesday, the court also called for an investigation into Rubio's dealings with a Swiss account which it said he had not sufficiently explained.
Rubio protested to journalists that it was "intolerable" that after four year of proceedings the court had decided to increase the charges.
